title: MuleSoft pricing: Is it worth it? [2026]
summary: MuleSoft pricing is anything but straightforward. Here's what you need to know about subscription tiers, vCores, and potential hidden costs before you sign up.
body_markdown:
MuleSoft has been around since the mid-2000s, back when developers like me were still stitching applications together using CSV file transfers and duct tape. It was one of the first dedicated data integration software packages on the market, and computer geeks loved that we could use it to program our interfaces and build complicated workflows.


Another reason we loved MuleSoft, called Mule ESB ([enterprise service bus](https://zapier.com/blog/enterprise-service-bus/) ) in those days, was that it was an open-source project. Not only could we use it to offload some of our integration work for free, we could also help code Mule itself. It was nerd heaven, I tell you.


Today, MuleSoft is as complex as ever, but the stakes are a lot higher. Now a full SaaS and[iPaaS](https://zapier.com/blog/what-is-ipaas/) (integration platform as a service) provider, it's far from free. In this guide, I'll step through how MuleSoft pricing works and compare that model to Zapier's so you can decide which is a better fit for your team.

## What is MuleSoft?


MuleSoft is an[enterprise-level integration and automation platform](https://zapier.com/blog/best-enterprise-integration-platforms/) that lets you connect APIs, apps, data, and systems across your organization and in the cloud. Founded in 2006, MuleSoft has long been a leader in the[business automation software](https://zapier.com/blog/business-automation-software/) space. It's owned by Salesforce and serves as a dedicated integration platform for connecting Salesforce across enterprise systems.


More recently, MuleSoft has branched out into AI. MuleSoft Vibes is an AI agent that helps you design, build, test, and operate integrations from natural-language requests, and MuleSoft's agent tools help you discover, connect, and govern agents built anywhere, including Salesforce's Agentforce agents.


MuleSoft's deep technical foundation lets developers build APIs and tightly control[integrations](https://zapier.com/blog/mulesoft-integrations) , but that complexity limits accessibility.


## MuleSoft pricing overview


[MuleSoft subscription costs](https://www.salesforce.com/mulesoft/anypoint-platform/pricing/) depend on which package you start with, how you choose to buy, and how many Mule Credits you use. It now publishes a starting price ($20,000/year), but anything beyond that depends on your package and buying model.


### MuleSoft Anypoint


The Anypoint Platform is MuleSoft's core offering, the entry point to its app and[data integration software](https://zapier.com/blog/data-integration-tools/) .


MuleSoft now sells Anypoint as five starting packages. Every package includes core platform capabilities and an allocation of Mule Credits, and the exact features and credit allocation depend on the package you pick. Packages start at $2,000 per month, billed annually.


Here's what each package is built for:


-


**Govern APIs and AI:** API and AI management, with out-of-the-box policies and guardrails and token budgets and cost controls. It covers 70 million or more API and model calls a year.


-


**Manage Agents:** Agent discovery and orchestration, agent governance, and token budgets and cost controls. It covers 180 million or more agent actions a year.


-


**Connect Apps:** Application integration, out-of-the-box connectors, and data connectivity. It covers 40 million or more records moved between apps a year.


-


**Process Documents:** Document automation, low-code workflows, and out-of-the-box connectors, to turn documents into structured data.


-


**Access Everything:** The full MuleSoft portfolio, covering 340 million or more calls across apps, APIs, and agents a year.


You can also choose how to buy.


-


**Pre-Purchase** means buying a package and credits up front, with no minimum credit purchase.


-


**Pre-Commit** requires a $50K minimum annual commitment and gives you one shared credit pool across products.


-


**Unlimited** is a custom fixed price with uncapped credits and full portfolio access. MuleSoft says rates drop as usage grows, by up to 90%.


Regardless of package, the starting price is just the beginning. MuleSoft measures usage in Mule Credits, a shared unit of consumption across eligible MuleSoft capabilities, and every package includes an allocation of them. How much you use determines what you actually pay.


### MuleSoft Vibes


MuleSoft Vibes is an[AI agent](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-agents-examples/) built into the MuleSoft platform that helps you design, build, test, and operate integrations from natural-language requests. It can generate flows, API specs, DataWeave transformations, and MUnit tests, reuse your existing assets, and connect to MCP servers. But it's still aimed at developers, admins, operations teams, and architects—it's not for the citizen developer.


Vibes is available to MuleSoft customers with an Anypoint subscription, and it doesn't require credits. (But check with the sales team on how the work Vibes kicks off is metered so you don't get any surprise charges.)


### MuleSoft and Agentforce


MuleSoft's Agentforce Connector lets developers integrate with agents running on Salesforce Agentforce: discover active agents, start agent sessions, and pass prompts from external applications to them. For managing agents more broadly, MuleSoft sells the Manage Agents package, which covers agent discovery and orchestration, agent governance, and token budgets and cost controls.


## Who is MuleSoft best for?


MuleSoft is best suited for large or growing companies with complex computing environments, enterprise-level architecture, and large, dedicated IT teams. MuleSoft can also play a key role for businesses building out a robust, long-term technology strategy. These organizations have the resources to make the most of a rich but complex platform.


It's an expansive automation ecosystem with very powerful capabilities that let you do just about anything you need with your integrations and workflows. That power and flexibility require both a heavy financial investment and deep technical knowledge, even as the company expands its AI offerings.


## MuleSoft vs. Zapier pricing


MuleSoft's pricing is more complicated than it looks. It publishes a $2,000-per-month starting price, but what you actually pay depends on the package you choose, how you buy, and how many Mule Credits you use. (The Unlimited buying model is a custom fixed price, which will be much higher than that $2,000/month tag.)


Zapier pricing, by contrast, is transparent. It's[task-based](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-pricing/) , and you'll only pay for tasks that actually complete work for you. Things like triggers, filters, and branching don't count against your task usage—and you certainly won't have to think about compute costs.


Zapier also actually publishes its prices. There's a Free plan with 100 tasks per month—no credit card required and no expiration. Paid plans start at $19.99/month for the Professional level, with 750 tasks per month. The Team package costs $69/month for up to 25 users and 2,000 tasks. You can upgrade to a custom Enterprise plan for higher limits and more security and governance features.


Regardless of which tier you choose on Zapier, you can start building workflows right away. It's a much faster start—and that's underselling it—than coding and connecting APIs with MuleSoft.


## Use Zapier for fewer barriers to integration and AI


MuleSoft's technical complexity means it takes a while to get up and running with your first integrations. And even then, you won't know exactly how much it's going to cost you since your credit usage depends on your package, your buying model, and what you build. By contrast, you can[sign up for Zapier right now](https://zapier.com/workflows) and have your first workflow live in no time at all—and you'll always know what it's going to cost you. (A lot less.)
